action: MS-ISAC advises applying Microsoft's updates after appropriate testing: SharePoint Server Subscription Edition 16.0.20326.20278 or later, and the fixed builds of Microsoft 365 Apps and Office LTSC 2021/2024 (Windows and Mac).
exec: MS-ISAC reports no exploitation of these SharePoint and Office flaws and rates the risk High for large and medium organisations.
plain: An advisory lists three flaws in Microsoft SharePoint and OneNote that could let an attacker run their own code. The advisory says no attacks are reported.

key_findings: SharePoint Server Subscription Edition before 16.0.20326.20278 and Office LTSC 2021 and 2024, Microsoft 365 Apps and Office for Mac before the listed builds are affected.
CVE-2026-124222 is improper authorisation and CVE-2026-124223 is deserialisation of untrusted data, both in SharePoint; CVE-2026-126526 is a heap overflow in OneNote.
The most severe could allow remote code execution with the privileges of the logged-on user.
There are no reports of exploitation in the wild.
Risk is High for large and medium government and business entities, Medium for small ones and Low for home users.
recommendations: Apply Microsoft's updates to vulnerable systems promptly after appropriate testing.
Run software as a non-administrative user and apply least privilege.
Segment the network and place internet-facing services in a DMZ.
Enable anti-exploitation features such as DEP and Windows Defender Exploit Guard.

summary: MS-ISAC advisory 2026-134, issued November 16, covers three Microsoft flaws: an improper authorisation bug and a deserialisation bug in SharePoint Server Subscription Edition, and a heap overflow in OneNote affecting Microsoft 365 Apps and Office LTSC 2021 and 2024 on Windows and Mac. The most severe could allow remote code execution; the advisory says an attacker could gain the logged-on user's privileges. It says there are no reports of exploitation in the wild.
title: MS-ISAC: Microsoft SharePoint and OneNote flaws could allow remote code execution
